lede: Jonas, the disobedient prophet, is swallowed by a whale on the high seas and remains there for three days, in a camera obscura. Barja, the artist-tumult-maker, returns the visitor to that belly: projected waters, open monads, word and image in suspension.
about.0: Jonas takes up the gesture that runs through Wagner Barja’s trajectory: to displace things from their place and reorder them. The prophet who disobeys and is swallowed by the whale is the visitor himself — returned to a belly of a camera obscura, where projected waters, open monads and words in suspension reorganize perception.
about.1: The installation was created for Experiência Tumulto III (CCBB Brasília, 2015) and documented in the final pages of the catalogue, with essays by Maria Thereza Azevedo (“Jonas: displacements and repetitions in multimedia installation”) and by Antônio Miranda (“Verbivocovisuality in the installation Jonas”). The water texture that runs across this page is the same one that was projected in the space of the installation.

trecho.1: artistic of Wagner Barja, an artist based in the federal capital. The exhibition reveals a “highly cohesive” oeuvre that, constituted over three decades, has always been marked by its experimental, irreverent and reflective character, by its transit through various media and artistic languages, by the crossing of different domains, bodies of knowledge and sensibilities. The exhibition comprises thirty works that make evident the diverse languages with which the artist works – visual poetry, videos and photographs, sculptures and installations, performances and urban interventions – and with a previously unseen installation, “Jonas”. In producing this anthology, the Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil makes it possible for the public to experience contemporary art through new languages, contributes to the education and democratization of culture and values local artistic production. Barja, the artist-tumult-maker, vomits the whale’s vertebrae, but before that, he digs into the bone to inject/nest images, pouring and inverting memories of waters into that which gives the bodies their support. trecho.5: deep, shallow, murky, calm, violent, red. Water, generator of life and of crossing, does not cease to dissolve and to transform itself. Bachelard recalls that the dreamer of water is a being in vertigo who constantly lets something of himself collapse. For him water is matter that is always about to become another. Hybrids and the out-of-place provoke estrangement, as the mythical monsters of the Middle Ages or Marcel Duchamp’s ready-mades provoked. They cause tumult, un-repair, de-stabilize and lead to rearrangements in our perception. Synthesis work of the exhibition Experiência Tumulto III, Jonas carries the artist’s trajectory, who has been practising displacements since Deitado Eternamente of 1986. It is a taking of things out of place and reordering, but not without first passing through the entrails of the anthropophagic tumult, which may instigate territories of existence and alter the hegemonic modes of subjectivation. In the witches’ cauldron of contemporary art, potions are stirred that mix procedures brought from art history.
